findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and raises TypeError when instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty `pass` body, but StatefulDetectorHandler has four abstract members it does not implement: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Under ABCMeta, instantiating the class raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. That instantiation happens in `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`) for any Detector whose type slug is `metric_alert_fire`, and the TypeError is not caught in `process_detectors`, so it would abort processing of the entire detector batch. Before this PR the class implemented `evaluate` itself and was instantiable. Either keep it on DetectorHandler until the stateful pieces exist, or implement the abstract hooks; the stale comment "This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction" should also be updated since the class now subclasses the stateful handler.

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) raises ValueError for DetectorPriorityLevel.CRITICAL
findings.body: In `evaluate_group_key_value`, the new occurrence branch converts the detector status via `PriorityLevel(new_status)`. `DetectorPriorityLevel` (sentry.workflow_engine.types) includes `CRITICAL = 100`, but `sentry.types.group.PriorityLevel` only defines LOW=25, MEDIUM=50, HIGH=75. The conversion works for LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH only because DetectorPriorityLevel is an IntEnum with matching values; if a detector's DataCondition has `condition_result=DetectorPriorityLevel.CRITICAL` and it fires, `new_status` becomes CRITICAL and `PriorityLevel(...)` raises `ValueError: 100 is not a valid PriorityLevel`. The exception propagates out of `handler.evaluate` and through `process_detectors`, killing the whole detector-processing loop and discarding the enqueued dedupe/state updates for that packet. The status should be validated/mapped before conversion (or CRITICAL condition results rejected for detectors), and `PriorityLevel(new_status.value)` would make the intended int conversion explicit.

findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected occurrence for the wrong group key and fails
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe`, the expected result is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, which embeds the fingerprint `"<detector.id>:val1"` via `build_fingerprint`. The code under test is then invoked with group key `"group_key"` (`handler.evaluate_group_key_value(expected_result.group_key, ...)`), so the occurrence actually produced by the handler has fingerprint `"<detector.id>:group_key"`. Both `DetectorEvaluationResult` and `IssueOccurrence` are dataclasses compared field by field, so the fingerprints differ and the `== expected_result` assertion fails deterministically. This worked before the PR only because the expected result had `result=None`. Build the expected occurrence with `"group_key"` (and matching value 10) instead of `"val1"`.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring on `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` reads "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`.", but this PR changed the method (and the abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature, and `process_detectors`) to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. The docstring should describe the dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores its `value` argument, hiding value mismatches in several tests
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, group_key, value, new_status)` never uses the `value` parameter when constructing the IssueOccurrence or event_data. Several updated tests depend on this: `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` evaluates value 8 but builds the expectation with 6, `TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change` evaluates 100 but expects 6, and `test_state_results_multi_group` evaluates `group_2` with value 10 but builds the expected occurrence with 6. Because the value is silently dropped, the suite cannot catch `evaluate_group_key_value` passing the wrong `value` into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Include the value in the mock's evidence_data (or assert it separately) so these mismatches would fail the tests.
